clue.text: US rock star encountered crossing a lounge

indicators.note: a word crossing another straddles it, so the next word sits inside the first

parts.note: met means encountered
taken as written
to loaf is to lounge about idly

explanation.surface: A fan bumps into an American rock singer while walking through a hotel lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lounge' looks like a room in the surface, but here it is a verb meaning to laze about.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat Loaf was the stage name of the American singer famous for the album Bat Out of Hell.

clue.text: Angry mother describing parking in NE town

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so one set of letters encloses another
an angry person is worked up and disordered, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A furious mum circles a parking space somewhere in the north-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: MORPETH is a market town in Northumberland, in the north-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Morpeth is the county town of Northumberland, which lies in England's north-east corner.

clue.text: Bill, artist in African capital

parts.note: ACC is short for account, a bill to be paid
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A man called Bill, a painter, lives in an African capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana in West Africa.

clue.text: The Parisian, so hot running in African country

parts.note: le is French for the, as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: running water moves about freely, so these letters flow into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman, finding the heat oppressive, goes jogging in an African land.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a small mountain kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Fruit, fish and vegetable retailer, initially

parts.note: an anchovy is a small salty fish
a pea is a vegetable

indicators.note: initially points at only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of retailer

explanation.surface: A list of what a market stallholder sells: fruit, fish and veg.
explanation.walkthrough: The anchovy pear is a West Indian fruit tree's fruit, eaten pickled like a mango.
explanation.definitionFit: The anchovy pear is a tropical fruit from the Caribbean tree Grias cauliflora.

clue.text: Training on first of April, leader of Dambusters took off

indicators.note: first of points at only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the opening letter of April
PE is physical education, training in school

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the opening letter of Dambusters

explanation.surface: Bomber crews train on the first of April before their squadron leader takes off on a raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took off' looks like an aircraft leaving, but here it means mimicked. 'On' places PE after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to impersonate them, which is a synonym for having imitated or mimicked.

clue.text: Saw lead choking dog?

indicators.note: something choking another grips it round the throat, so it encloses it

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
Rover is a stock name for a dog

explanation.surface: Is a tight leash strangling the dog?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like a dog lead; it is the metal. 'Saw' is the noun meaning an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, the same thing as a proverb.

clue.text: Cup of tea? Missed out

indicators.note: out can mean out of place or wrong, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks if you'd like a cup of tea and you didn't get one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cup of tea' looks like one phrase, but 'Cup' alone is the definition and 'of' joins it to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A demitasse is a small coffee cup, from French for half-cup.

clue.text: Crouch down by bed to get large bag

parts.note: in dialect, to ruck is to squat or crouch
the sack is slang for bed, as in hit the sack

explanation.surface: A camper squats by a sleeping bag to pack a big backpack.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack is a large bag carried on the back by hikers.

clue.text: Style, class to a T

parts.note: a form is a school class
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's style is described as classy, down to a T.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To a T' is an idiom meaning exactly, but here A and T are just letters added.
explanation.definitionFit: A format is the style or arrangement in which something is presented.

clue.text: Close to tent, spots rubbish

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of tent
a rash is a breakout of spots

explanation.surface: A camper notices spots of litter near the tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Trash is the American word for rubbish or refuse.

clue.text: Demand made by former partner to behave

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to act is to behave in a certain way

explanation.surface: An ex-partner demands better behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to demand or insist on payment or compliance.

clue.text: Love playing Chartres in big band

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, a round O

indicators.note: playing with something moves it around, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician loves performing in Chartres, the French cathedral town, with a big band.
explanation.walkthrough: Chartres is a French city with a famous cathedral; here it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large ensemble of musicians, so a big band in the literal sense.

clue.text: Forge iron bar initially on it

indicators.note: initially says the word just before it goes at the front of the build

parts.note: a counter is a bar where drinks or goods are served
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
taken as written

explanation.surface: A blacksmith forges an iron bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' does not take a first letter: it says bar's word comes first, before iron and it.
explanation.definitionFit: To counterfeit is to forge or fake something such as money or documents.

clue.text: Dutch painter depicting seedy boys' home with urchins

indicators.note: something seedy is run down and shabby, so these letters are in disarray

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Dutch artist paints a squalid boys' home full of street children.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a description of a painting, apt for a painter of grotesque scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieronymus Bosch was a Netherlandish painter famed for The Garden of Earthly Delights.

clue.text: Moving, English poet to Alabama

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
Andrew Motion was the UK Poet Laureate from 1999 to 2009
AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama

explanation.surface: An English poet relocates to Alabama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' suggests relocating, which suits the surface, but it means stirring the feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moving touches the heart, so it is emotional.

clue.text: Throughout most of term, terribly strict

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so these letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
stern means strict

explanation.surface: A teacher has been very strict for most of the school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' looks like an instruction to drop a letter, but the words are taken whole as anagram letters.
explanation.definitionFit: From stem to stern is an idiom meaning from one end of a ship to the other, hence entirely.

clue.text: Warning about onset of thunder (loud)

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its beginning, so just its first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of thunder

explanation.surface: A storm warning: the thunder is starting, and it's loud.
explanation.walkthrough: Fore! is shouted on a golf course to warn players a ball is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: Forte is the musical direction meaning to play loudly.

clue.text: Disappointed, no end, having received a bronze — that's diabolical

indicators.note: something that has received another holds it within
having no end means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: sick as a parrot is British slang for bitterly disappointed
a tan is a bronze colour on the skin

explanation.surface: An athlete missing out on the top prize and settling for bronze calls it diabolical.
explanation.walkthrough: SICK loses its end to become SIC, which then takes in A TAN. 'Bronze' looks like a medal; here it is a suntan.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic means devilish, like Satan, so it is a synonym of diabolical.

clue.text: Warriors will achieve odd reversal in Asia, possibly

indicators.note: a reversal turns things back to front, so the word before it reads backwards
in places one word inside the other
possibly means in some possible version, so these letters may be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Warriors will pull off a strange turnaround in Asia, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Samurai were the hereditary warrior class of feudal Japan; the word serves as its own plural.

clue.text: Most closely related are placed in home

indicators.note: something placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a nest is a home
taken as written

explanation.surface: Your closest relatives are the ones living in your home.
explanation.definitionFit: Next of kin are one's nearest relatives, nearest meaning most closely related.

clue.text: Terrorise giddy merrymaker

indicators.note: a giddy person spins about, so these letters whirl into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dizzy reveller frightens people.
explanation.definitionFit: A roisterer is a noisy reveller, someone who parties boisterously.

clue.text: Number one cricket club with a hallowed ground

parts.note: number one is oneself, me
CC is the abbreviation for cricket club
taken as written

explanation.surface: A top cricket club owns a famous, revered ground, like Lord's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' looks like a ranking; it is the speaker. 'Ground' sounds like a cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Mecca is the holiest city of Islam, so by extension any place revered or sought after.

clue.text: Group of activists worry about introduction of democracy

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: care means worry

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: the first letter of democracy

explanation.surface: Political activists fret about bringing democracy in.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a core group of trained activists in a political party or movement.

clue.text: Warm current in lake, one abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or widely scattered, so these letters are spread into new positions

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warm current flows into a lake somewhere overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One abroad' tempts a foreign word like uno, and Spanish El Niño fits that idea, but the letters come from a straight anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: El Niño is a periodic warming of Pacific Ocean currents off South America.

clue.text: Book, say, with Dickens character causing envy

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book
e.g. means for example, or say
Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: A Dickens novel featuring a character who stirs up jealousy.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge is to envy someone something, resenting that they have it.

clue.text: Lost, excellent fabric

parts.note: L stands for lost, as in a sports results table
ace is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: Some fine fabric has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lace is a delicate openwork textile, a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Small ballistic missile, ear-piercing

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
Trident is the submarine-launched ballistic missile carried by the UK and US

explanation.surface: A small ballistic missile makes a deafening noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident sound is harsh and loud, so it pierces the ear.
